{{Top|leg|canon=Galactic Barrier}}
{{Youmay|the barrier that divides the Unknown Regions from the rest of the galaxy|the [[circumferential hyperspace barrier]] that surrounds the galaxy}}
{{Quote|It once extended across the entire galaxy, dividing it in two, but is now decaying and gradually retreating toward the Core.|Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]]|<ref name="Author's Cut">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref>}}
[[File:Western_barrier.jpg|thumb|right|350px|The chain of hyperspace anomalies prevented exploration of Unknown Regions]]
The '''western barrier''', also known as the '''western anomalies''',<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the '''hyperspace tangle''',<ref name="EotE">[[Star Wars: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Edge of the Empire'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> or just '''the tangle''',<ref name="TUR">''[[The Unknown Regions]]''</ref> was a chain of [[Hyperspace anomaly/Legends|hyperspace anomalies]] that bisected [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] west of the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] and prevented exploration of the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]] for millennia. It formed the midline of the [[circumferential hyperspace barrier]] that enveloped the galaxy in a shell of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] turbulence.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Though the barrier was believed to have once spanned the length of the galaxy, it had frayed and decayed over millennia in its gradual retreat back towards the galactic core.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Description==
{{Quote|General, when you were a child did you ever have a spinning top? One with a string?''"''<br />''"''It’s been a while, Doctor, but I’m familiar with the concept.''"''<br />''"''Imagine that our galaxy is a child’s top, and what we call the circumferential barrier is a collection of countless whorls and eddies spinning around it too quickly to safely traverse at faster-than-light speeds. I believe the Celestials spun up that barrier by tapping the energies of the galactic center. The western barrier, essentially, is what’s left of the string.|Dr. Insmot Bowen and [[General/Legends|General]] [[Arhul Kurumenga]]|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
Like the circumferential hyperspace barrier, the western barrier was believed by the [[Pre-Republic era|Pre-Republic]] specialists, including Dr. [[Insmot Bowen]] of the [[Obroan Institute for Archaeology]], to be constructed by the [[Celestial/Legends|Celestials]]. Speculation holds that the Celestials had crafted the [[Hyperspace anomaly/Legends|hyperspace anomalies]] that bisected the galaxy during the [[Rakatan revolt]] in order to contain the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> with the help of their servants, the [[Gree (species)/Legends|Gree]], the [[Kwa/Legends|Kwa]], and the [[Killik/Legends|Killiks]].<ref name="EGtW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Others believed that the barrier was of natural origins thanks to the "hyperspatial gravitic ripples"<ref name="TEA" /> or that it have been created by the Celestials as a defensive measure against [[Mnggal-Mnggal]] and its infectious intentions, separating Celestial projects in the eastern disk near [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] and other sites.<ref name="TUR" />

Despite its reputation as the hyperspace equivalent of a jagged-edged reef, the anomaly line was demonstrably permeable<ref name="TEA" />&mdash;for instance, [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] traders had been in contact with the [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] for many years before their "re-discovery",<ref name="OBF">[[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']]</ref> the planet [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]] was reachable by [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] navigators,<ref name="TEA" /> the Rakata homeworld of [[Lehon/Legends|Lehon]] was also reached by a [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic naval]] task force at the climax of the [[Jedi Civil War]]<ref name="KOTOR">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref> and subsequently made a protected historical site by the Republic. Additionally, frontier spaceport worlds in the known galaxy, like [[Terminus/Legends|Terminus]], were known to be visited frequently by transports and traders from the Unknown Regions.<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
The hyperspace travel to other galaxies was long thought impossible due to [[circumferential hyperspace barrier]]. In [[27 BBY/Legends|27 BBY]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Jorus C'baoth]] believed that the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] could use [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to smooth this zone of turbulence and allow the vessel to pass. He demonstrated this technique on the briarpatch border of the Unknown Regions, and then recommended that eighteen Jedi, including himself, be included in the [[Outbound Flight Project]].<ref name="The New Essential Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>

In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], a debriefing on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], held by Dr. Insmot Bowen of the Obroan Institute for Archaeology and attended by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Arhul Kurumenga]] of the [[Imperial Department of Military Research/Legends|Imperial Department of Military Research]], [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] of the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]], and [[Master of Imperial Projects]] [[Bevel Lemelisk]] discussed the possible origins of the western barrier.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The hyperspace anomaly was in fact something that I helped create during the development of the original Star Wars galaxy maps in the late 1990s. Even at that time, the existence of an Unknown Regions within the galactic disc was established as a given. Trying to establish an internal logic for why an Unknown Regions would exist at all, I hit on hyperspace and the truism that traveling through it ain't like dusting crops. While hyperspace disturbances are generally tied to real-world objects and their mass shadows, that doesn't mean they always need to be - we're talking about an alternate dimension after all - and appealing to the enigma of hyperspatial physics helped establish three things: (1) why there was an Unknown Regions, (2) why the galaxy had "superhighways," and (3) why nobody had traveled outside the galaxy and made a start at establishing a multi-galaxy civilization. (No, the satellite galaxies don't count.)|Daniel Wallace|<ref name="Danblog TEA">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_24.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 2 of 5)}}</ref>}}
[[Daniel Wallace]], one of the authors of [[The Unknown Regions]] sourcebook, hinted that the hyperspace boundary was created by the Celestials in order to protect themselves from the Mnggal-Mnggal.<ref name="Danblog TUR">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2010/04/endnotes-for-star-wars-unknown-regions.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Unknown Regions}}</ref>
